Q: How to properly serialize raw binary data in C/C++? A:

To my knowledge, there is no preferred method of serialization and deserialization. Most people say to use a library.
I prefer using a uint8_t array, copying the data to the array (serializing) or extracting the data from the array (deserializing), then using block write (serializing) or block read (deserializing). I usually put the buffer read and write in the objects because the objects know the sizes of the members.

Keep in mind that compression and encryption are similar but different techniques.

Q: Convert multiline string to array A:

Let me contribute to Sanket Parmar's answer. If you can extract string splitting and processing into a separate function, there is no need to save and restore $IFS — use local instead:

#!/bin/bash

function print_with_line_numbers {
    local IFS=$'\n'
    local lines=($1)
    local i
    for (( i=0; i<${#lines[@]}; i++ )) ; do
        echo "$i: ${lines[$i]}"
    done
}

names="Netgear
Hon Hai Precision Ind. Co.
Apple"

print_with_line_numbers "$names"

See also:

  • Setting IFS for a single statement

UPD:

Unfortunately, this very approach contains a fatal flaw: here, local lines=($1) does not just split the string, but also performs glob expansion. So, if the string contains a glob expression, it will be expanded:

$ str="/*" ; arr=($str) ; echo "${arr[@]}"
/bin /boot /dev /etc /home /init /lib /media /mnt ...

Q: Azure Login via GitHub Actions fails with "No subscriptions found" using Student Subscription A:

If you do not need access to the subscription, you can add allow-no-subscriptions: true to the list of inputs:

      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
        uses: azure/login@532459ea530d8321f2fb9bb10d1e0bcf23869a43 #v3.0.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          allow-no-subscriptions: true

If you do need access to the subscription, make sure the Service principal has the subscription assigned. You can do that by assigning a role to the App Registration:

# Get your app registration's client ID
APP_CLIENT_ID="<your-app-registration-client-id>"

# Get your subscription ID
SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)

# Assign Reader role at subscription scope
az role assignment create \
  --assignee "$APP_CLIENT_ID" \
  --role "Reader" \
  --scope "/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID"

Q: Designing a Python API: list of coordinate tuples vs separate parameters? A:

Use a list if there can be an arbitrary number of coordinates. Use separate parameters if the number is fixed.

Although you can also use a spread parameter in the case of an arbitrary number:

def route(*coords: list[tuple[float, float]]):
    ...

Q: Looking for a new API that is for geolocating for the UK A:

I built a free UK postcode geocoder API which you can access here:

https://www.getthedata.com/open-postcode-geo-api
